proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 5, 2.4 (derived there from 4.7 and 4.9 of Ch. 4), in the corrected form (P.i)-(P.ii) of the parent proof, with Lambda = 4p delta/(p-n).

Notation. mu := V.weight, omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0, kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0, Lambda_t := 4pt/(p-n) = t/kappa for t >= 0, B_s(y) closed balls.

1. Choice of delta_P. The functions g_+(t) := e^(2 Lambda_t)(1+t)(1-3t)^-n + 2 e^(Lambda_t) Lambda_t/omega_n and g_-(t) := e^(-Lambda_t)(1 - Lambda_t/omega_n) are continuous on [0, 1/8] with g_+(0) = g_-(0) = 1. Choose delta_P with 0 < delta_P <= min{1/8, kappa} such that g_+(t) <= 2 and g_-(t) >= 1/2 for all t in [0, delta_P].
2. Let 0 < delta <= delta_P, 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2. Put Lambda := Lambda_delta = 4p delta/(p-n); then Lambda <= 1 (delta <= kappa). Put R_y := (1 - 3 delta) rho >= 5 rho/8 > rho/2 >= s. Then B_(R_y)(y) is contained in B_rho(0), since |x| <= |y| + R_y <= rho for x in B_(R_y)(y). Hence the monotonicity child (lip_approx_monotonicity) applies with this Lambda, centre y and radius R = R_y.
3. Upper bound. For every r in [s, R_y), the first assertion of the monotonicity child gives mu(B_s(y))/s^n <= e^(2 Lambda) mu(B_r(y))/r^n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda, and mu(B_r(y)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n by 2.3 (B_r(y) is contained in B_rho(0)). The right side e^(2 Lambda)(1 + delta) omega_n rho^n r^-n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda is continuous in r; letting r increase to R_y gives mu(B_s(y))/s^n <= e^(2 Lambda)(1 + delta) omega_n (1 - 3 delta)^-n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda = omega_n g_+(delta) <= 2 omega_n. Since mu(B_s(y)) < infinity (compact subset of U), this is the inequality V.weight(closedBall y s) <= ofReal(2 omega_n s^n).
4. Lower bound. Let y in spt V. The third assertion of the monotonicity child (with r := s, so s <= r < R_y) gives mu(B_s(y))/s^n >= e^(-Lambda)(omega_n - Lambda) = omega_n g_-(delta) >= omega_n/2, i.e. ofReal(omega_n s^n/2) <= V.weight(closedBall y s).
